title: Six looks for the same world, at 8x and at play scale
question: The aesthetic is on the table, not just the zoom: which of these looks should this game have -- A cell-art (today), B soft, C illustrated, D painted, E lit, F textured cell-art? Pick one; say what it gets wrong. The last pane shows all six at 3x, which is where a look has to hold.
context_md:
Same world, same crop, same 1:1 colours in every pane. Nothing in the simulation changes for any of them -- each is a rule for which *class* (air / water / soil / stone / plant) a sub-pixel belongs to and which cell it takes its colour from, so no pane can invent a colour the engine would not draw.

- **A cell-art** -- today: every cell a flat square.
- **B soft** -- bilinear between cell centres. At 3x the thin twigs go to haze.
- **C illustrated** -- curved silhouettes, flat interiors that keep their grain, an ink line where a mass meets air. At 3x every twig is bolder than today.
- **D painted** -- soft, with a fine grain laid back over it.
- **E lit** -- illustrated plus edge shading from the shape itself: leaves become beads, the pool gets a bevel. This is the 3d-ish look you turned down for plants in August; it is here so it is turned down on purpose.
- **F textured cell-art** -- the pixel look kept, with each material drawn up close the way it looks at 1x (grain, bark, leaf lobes) and the water surface drawn as a level rather than a dark line.

**My reading, which is the thing to check:** C is the one look that is a *different game* rather than the same game filtered, it is the cheapest of the non-pixel looks, and it is the only one that keeps more definition than today at play scale. B and D lose thin things at 3x -- your zoom-out complaint by another route. If the pixel look stays, F.

Whichever wins ships as a runtime selector with its dials on the parameters page, not as a chosen constant. Cost under each pane is extra work per output pixel over today, from one quiet run; every look keeps the settled-world render skip.
